slides.title: Two servers run the same job. **Who gets the lock?**
slides.text: SETNX, Redlock and the big debate 👉

slides.title: The **naive** lock
slides.text: Two commands. Crash between them and the lock never expires.
slides.code:
SETNX lock 1
   💥 crash here
EXPIRE lock 30
→ locked forever ❌

slides.title: One **atomic** command
slides.text: NX = only if absent. PX = TTL. Token = who owns it.
slides.code:
SET lock:order:42 <token> NX PX 30000

-- release (Lua)
if get(key) == token
then del(key) end

slides.title: Locks can **lie**
bullets: ⏳|TTL expires during a GC pause: two holders

cols.title: 🛡 Redlock
cols.text: Survives losing 1 or 2 nodes. Fine in practice.

cols.title: 🧐 Kleppmann
cols.text: Timing assumptions break. No fencing token. Use etcd / ZooKeeper for correctness.

slides.title: What do you need?
bullets: 🧹|**Efficiency** (avoid duplicate work): one Redis lock is fine
🗄️|Or skip locks: DB row lock or version check

slides.title: Say this in 1 line
slides.text: Lock with **SET NX PX + token**, release with a **Lua check**. For efficiency that is enough; for correctness use **fencing tokens** or **etcd/ZooKeeper**, not Redlock alone.

slides.text: Fixed window, sliding window, token bucket. Follow and save 🔖
